name: Structure Quality
description: Scores how well a project's code and records divide the work, so scoping and modularity are judged by a number and its worst offenders instead of by whoever reads the whole tree: one job per solution, parts small and simple enough to read, connections only through declared entry points or the project's shared kernel, no copied code, a public surface that is used, and behavior held by a contract that runs every arm.
purpose: Measure how well a project divides its work into solutions and parts, as one balanced number with the worst offenders named, before and after code exists.
approach: Read the code and records without running them, score seven dimensions (scope, size, coupling, reuse, flow fidelity, public surface, behavior preserved) against budgets fixed beforehand, graded by how far a part goes over its budget where size is concerned, with the project's shared kernel told apart from another solution's internals, weight them into one number no single dimension can win, and mine the git history for files that change together across solutions as a second, more faithful stage of the same number.
out_of_scope: Running the structural rules on each change; deciding whether a rule earns its place; the correctness of what any one part produces; deciding that a solution's purpose is worth having.
milestones: 1. Stage one scores every dimension offline on small cases and on whole repositories. [met: 2026-11-05] 2. Stage two reads co-change from git history. [met: 2026-11-05] 3. The expert review of scoping is specified and costed, not run. [met: 2026-11-05] 4. A consumer states its own budgets and cases on top of this metric and keeps no copy of the scorer.
knowledge: Ousterhout on deep modules and pass-through methods; Parnas on information hiding; Martin's instability metric and the stable dependencies, acyclic dependencies, common reuse and interface segregation principles (the shared kernel and the fat interface); McCabe's cyclomatic complexity; PEP 8 on a package's __init__ as its interface; clone detection by token windows; logical coupling from co-change in version history (Gall, Zimmermann); esoi's own S48, S49 and coherence evidence.
measures_of_success: The balanced number agrees with labelled structural incidents: a clean exemplar is sound, each incident flags the dimension it damages, and the project cut into tiny files scores below the balanced real structure that a size-only scorer prefers. Standing conditions: weights and budgets are fixed before any alternative is scored; a dimension that cannot be measured is reported as not measured, never as perfect; findings inform and never fail a check.
parameters: The project path, the stage (1 static, 2 adds history), and the budgets a consumer may tighten (function and module lines, complexity per function, files per folder, solutions per intent, depth, Protocols per unit, the clone window, the importers and instability of a shared kernel, the consumers a library must not name).
inputs: The project's Python files, its records beside the code, its test files, the coherence gate's report where records exist, and at stage two its git history.
outputs: One balanced number from 0 to 1, each dimension's score, the dimensions flagged and each one's worst offenders
effects: None: it reads and reports. Structure Check's advisory rules print its findings.
usage_notes: Run `esoi structure-quality [--stage 1|2] [path]`. Weights are fixed in `balance.py`; a consumer tightens budgets and adds cases, never a copy of the scorer (`[builds_on]`). A single-factor score such as file size alone is the bound the balanced number must beat, since shrinking files wins it.
